revision_notes: Confirmed as of 2026: no hyperscale cloud provider (AWS, Azure, GCP, Huawei, Oracle) operates a region in Congo or Central Africa; the only African hyperscale regions remain in South Africa, a different sub-region, so 'served remotely from distant regions only' is accurate. Value unchanged at 2 but now evidence-based rather than uncited.

Definition: The presence and tier quality of commercial/colocation data center facilities operating in the country. Commercial data centers provide the physical infrastructure for hosting cloud services, content delivery, and enterprise applications domestically.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: MTN Congo operates a commercial colocation data centre in Brazzaville (registered on PeeringDB) and Congo Telecom runs a carrier facility in Pointe-Noire, directly contradicting the 'no commercial data centers' claim. No Tier III/IV certification found for any facility, so revised to 2 (small-scale facilities only, Tier I-II) rather than confirming 1.

Definition: Whether the government has established dedicated data center infrastructure and/or a government cloud (G-Cloud) strategy for hosting e-government services and public sector data domestically. Critical for data sovereignty and e-government service delivery.
Value Name: No government data center or cloud strategy
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Congo adopted a national digital strategy ('Vision Congo Digital 2025', approved 2019, referencing public/private/hybrid cloud models) and already operates government data centres via regulator ARPCE in Brazzaville (since 2021) and Pointe-Noire (launched Feb 2026), so 'no strategy/data center' is false. A larger AfDB-funded flagship national data centre (90%+ complete by Aug 2025) was targeted for operational launch by May 2026 per Feb 2026 reporting, but no source confirms it has actually gone live; revised conservatively to 3 (basic government data center operational, strategy adopted) rather than 4, and flagged for human review to confirm the flagship centre's live status closer to the current date.
